lines.text: Later it cools off. Management has been informed and does not care.
Later it cools off. Every 'quick walk' out there just got quicker.
Later it cools off. Not by much. Just enough to be petty about it.
Later it cools off. Every hand out there goes into a pocket, like they're all hiding something.
Later it cools off. I say that so often, it's going on my headstone.
Later it cools off. The line at the ice cream place shrinks to the truly committed.
Later it cools off. I'm not supposed to enjoy saying that.
Later it cools off. The cats worked that out hours ago.
Later it cools off. In lieu of flowers, the warm part of the day asks for sweaters.
Warm, then cold again. Please keep all layers with you until the ride comes to a complete stop.
Warm, then cold again. I'd explain it, but the weather didn't explain it to me either.
Warm, then cold again. Twice the weather, same pay. Which is nothing.
Warm, then cold again. Days like this are 11% of my work and 80% of the complaints.
Warm, then cold again. A day built by someone who's never had to dress for it.
Warm, then cold again. Expect a big rise in people saying 'it's deceiving out there.'
Warm, then cold again. The weather thinks this is a fun bit. It isn't.
Warm, then cold again. The thermometer on the bank sign gets to be the busiest screen in town. Show-off.
Warm, then cold again. Every sweater in town gets its neck stretched twice.
Warm, then cold again. The warm part lasts about one ice cream cone.
Warm, then cold again. Lost: the warm part of the day. Last seen in the middle. No reward.
Warm, then cold again. Every toddler in town gets wrestled out of a jacket and back into it, screaming both times.
Later it warms up. The cold was only the opening act. Nobody came for the opening act.
Later it warms up. The weather started cold just to make the rest look generous.
Later it warms up. Good news, delivered by me. As usual, no tip.
Later it warms up. Some politician will probably take credit for it.
Later it warms up. The cold is being let go. No severance.
Later it warms up. The comeback nobody asked for, and everybody will take.
Later it warms up. Hats come off all over town. Brace for the hair.
Later it warms up. My approval rating should go up a few points.
Later it warms up. Half the town will walk around with a layer over one arm, like waiters.
Every umbrella out there will be held at exactly someone else's eye level.
The sky is undergoing maintenance. Expect leaks.
Confession: I've forecast so much rain, I've started rooting for it.
The rain always waits for someone to say 'I think it's stopping.'
Everyone out there will do that fast walk that refuses to be called running.
Every clogged gutter in town has been waiting for this.
Big day for the man who refuses to own an umbrella. He's proving a point to nobody.
Every worm in town will come up onto the sidewalk and immediately regret it.
Every phone in town will say '40%' and refuse to explain.
Warm, then cold again. You'll warm up a little in the middle. People will mistake it for personality.
Warm, then cold again. The day peaks in the middle. You peaked in high school.
Warm, then cold again. You'll look the same in every layer. That's not a compliment.
Warm, then cold again. Goosebumps, then sweat patches, then goosebumps. Quite the glow-up.
Warm, then cold again. The weather will be nice to you for a while, then remember who you are.
Warm, then cold again. You'll tell three people it's 'crazy weather.' None of them will care.
Warm, then cold again. A day that needs planning past lunch. Not your strong suit.
Warm, then cold again. You'll warm up for a while. Longer than your last hobby lasted.
Warm, then cold again. You'll look comfortable for a bit in the middle. Nobody will get a photo of it.
Warm, then cold again. You'll overheat in the middle and turn the color of a ham.
Warm, then cold again. Your layer will get more attention today than you have all year.
Warm, then cold again. A day like this needs someone flexible. You can't even touch your toes.
Warm, then cold again. In the warm part, you'll roll up your sleeves like you're about to do something. You won't.
Warm, then cold again. A day in two parts. You'll be forgettable in both.
Warm, then cold again. You'll spend the day fiddling with a zipper. Easily your most skilled work this week.
A T-shirt day. Finally, everyone gets to see what the winter coat was hiding.
A T-shirt day. Probably the free one from that fun run you mostly walked.
Perfect weather. Ideal conditions for you to be mildly disappointing outdoors, for a change.
A T-shirt day. Somebody out there is wearing the same shirt as you and doing it better.
Perfect weather. Every dog out there will enjoy today more than you've enjoyed anything.
A T-shirt day. You'll tuck it in, untuck it, and settle on halfway. Classic you.
Perfect weather. You'll still walk like you're late for something. You're not. Nobody's waiting.
A T-shirt day. You'll stand outside with your face up like a lizard with a mortgage.
A T-shirt day. You'll catch your reflection in a shop window and speed up.
Perfect weather. Everyone will be in a good mood. Even people who've met you.
A T-shirt day. If your shirt has words on it, it'll be the wittiest thing about you.
A T-shirt day. You'll stand up straight for the first ten minutes. Then you'll remember who you are.
Later it warms up. The weather gets a second act. You're still waiting on your first.
Later it warms up. Slow start, strong finish. You've got the first half down.
Later it warms up. You'll warm up too, eventually. People usually leave before that.
Later it warms up. You can stop walking like a folding chair.
Later it warms up. By then you'll have complained enough to deserve none of it.
Later it warms up. You'll step outside and blink like you've just been released.
Later it warms up. Enough to sit outside. Not enough to make you interesting.
Later it warms up. The layer comes off, and with it your excuse for that look.
Later it warms up. Finally, something near you is improving.
Later it warms up. You'll thaw out in stages, like a supermarket chicken.
Later it warms up. Your face will thaw out. Most people won't notice the difference.
Later it warms up. You'll finally unclench. Your jaw, anyway. Not your personality.
